questions.sub_topic: Algebra of Matrices
questions.question: If A = [[1, 2], [3, 4]] and B = [[5, 6], [7, 8]], what is the (1,2) entry of AB?
questions.explanation: The (1,2) entry of AB is the dot product of row 1 of A and column 2 of B: 1×6 + 2×8 = 6 + 16 = 22.

questions.sub_topic: Determinant of a square matrix (up to 3×3)
questions.question: \( If A = [[3, 1], [2, 4]], what is the value of \left| \1 \right|? \)
questions.explanation: \( \left| \1 \right| = 3×4 − 1×2 = 10. \left| \1 \right| = \left| \1 \right|² = 100. The determinant of a matrix squared equals the square of the determinant. \)

questions.sub_topic: Determinant of a square matrix (up to 3×3)
questions.question: If the determinant of [[a, b], [c, d]] is 8, what is the determinant of [[2a, 2b], [c, d]]?
questions.explanation: \( Multiplying the first row by 2 multiplies the determinant by 2. So \left| \1 \right| = 2 × 8 = 16. \)

questions.sub_topic: Conditional probability
questions.question: \( A fair die is rolled twice. What is the probability that the \sum of the two rolls is 7? \)
questions.explanation: \( There are 6 outcomes that give \sum 7: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1). Total outcomes = 36. P = \frac{6}{36} = \frac{1}{6}. \)

questions.sub_topic: Multiplication theorem on probability
questions.question: In how many ways can a committee of 3 be formed from 7 people?
questions.explanation: \( C(7,3) = 7!/(3!×4!) = (7×6×5)/(3×2×1) = 35. This is a combination problem since order does not matter \in a committee. \)

questions.explanation: Product rule: f'(x) = 3x²·eˣ + x³·eˣ = x²eˣ(3+x).

questions.question: \( If A is a 2×2 matrix with \left| \1 \right| = 0, which of the following is true? \)
options: C) A has a unique inverse
questions.explanation: \( A matrix with determinant zero is called singular and does not have an inverse. Only non-singular matrices (\left| \1 \right| ≠ 0) are invertible. \)

questions.explanation: \( For a 2×2 matrix [[a,b],[c,d]], the determinant is ad−bc. Here, \left| \1 \right| = 3^3 * \left| \1 \right| = 27 * 3 = 81. This gives the value of the determinant, which represents the area scaling factor of the linear transformation. \)
